description: Two-panel mechanical-property figure for Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C low-density steel after solution treatment at four temperatures, colour-coded black = 700 °C, red = 800 °C, blue = 900 °C, magenta = 1000 °C. (a) True stress (MPa, y axis 0–1200, 200 MPa ticks) versus true strain ε (x axis −0.05 to 0.40, 0.05 ticks). No yield-point drop is visible on any curve; the magenta 1000 °C curve rises extremely steeply and shows an almost vertical stress jump at very low strain; the blue 900 °C curve is lowest at small strain but crosses the others and ends at the highest stress level; rupture strains decrease in the order 800 °C ≈ 900 °C > 700 °C > 1000 °C. (b) Work-hardening rate dσ/dε (MPa, y axis 0–8000, 1000 MPa ticks) versus true strain for the same four conditions, annotated S1, S2, S3 with dashed vertical stage boundaries and arrow labels 700 °C, 800 °C, 900 °C, 1000 °C. All curves drop steeply in S1; magenta (1000 °C) collapses fastest, black (700 °C) shows a small S2 hump, red (800 °C) plateaus near the 1000–1500 gridlines, and blue (900 °C) sustains the highest S2 rate before a late S3 fall. Together the panels show that 900 °C solution treatment gives the best strength–ductility balance via sustained work hardening.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots true stress in MPa (y axis 0–1200, ticks every 200) against true strain ε (x axis from −0.05 to 0.40, ticks every 0.05).
Panel (a) contains four curves labelled at their upper ends as 700 °C (black), 800 °C (red), 900 °C (blue) and 1000 °C (magenta).

The blue 900 °C curve reaches the highest true stress of the four conditions, terminating above the 1000 MPa gridline at the largest strain, while the magenta 1000 °C curve terminates first, between the 0.10 and 0.15 strain gridlines.
The magenta 1000 °C curve in (a) rises almost vertically at the lowest strains, showing a near-vertical stress jump below ε = 0.02; the other three curves show no such jump.
No yield-point drop (yield-point phenomenon) is visible on any of the four curves in (a); every curve rises monotonically from the origin.

Panel (b) plots the work-hardening rate dσ/dε (y axis 0–8000 MPa, ticks every 1000) against true strain ε (same x axis as (a)), with the same four colour-coded conditions labelled 700 °C, 800 °C, 900 °C and 1000 °C by arrows.
Panel (b) marks three work-hardening stages S1, S2 and S3 with dashed vertical boundary lines; all four curves decrease steeply in S1.

In panel (b) the blue 900 °C curve shows the highest plateau in stage 2, rising from about the 2000 MPa level to a broad maximum approaching the 3000 MPa gridline, whereas the magenta 1000 °C curve falls to zero earliest, near ε ≈ 0.13.
Fig. 2 consists of (a) true stress-strain curves and (b) work hardening rate.
The citing text states that no yield point phenomenon occurs under all the solution treatment conditions.

The citing text states that with increasing solution temperature both the critical stress for uniform deformation and the work hardening rate decreased obviously — this ranking conflicts with the visual reading that the 900 °C (blue) curve has the highest flow stress and the highest sustained stage-2 hardening rate.

The citing text asserts that for H90 the true stress increased abruptly at a true strain of ~0.03 and that both UTS and TE were the highest among the four steels; in the pixels the abrupt low-strain stress jump belongs to the magenta 1000 °C curve, not the 900 °C curve, so the label-to-curve assignment cannot be resolved from the figure alone.

The citing text describes a three-stage work-hardening behaviour (stage 1 rapid decrease associated with ferrite deformation, stage 2 slight decrease from TRIP/TWIP-type hardening, stage 3 rapid decrease from deformation localization), matching the S1/S2/S3 annotations drawn in panel (b).

subfigures.description: True stress (MPa) vs true strain ε for four solution-treatment temperatures: black 700 °C, red 800 °C, blue 900 °C, magenta 1000 °C. All curves start rising from the origin with no yield-point drop; magenta rises exceptionally steeply with an abrupt near-vertical jump at very low strain and ends first, around ε ≈ 0.13–0.15 just below the 1000 MPa gridline; black 700 °C ends near ε ≈ 0.18 below the 1000 MPa gridline; red 800 °C extends to about the 0.28 gridline at roughly 950 MPa; blue 900 °C extends slightly further and reaches the highest stress of the group, above the 1000 MPa gridline.

Work-hardening rate dσ/dε (MPa, 0–8000) vs true strain ε (−0.05 to 0.40) for the same four conditions, with stage markers S1, S2 and S3 and dashed vertical boundary lines, plus arrow/label annotations 700 °C (black), 800 °C (red), 900 °C (blue), 1000 °C (magenta). All curves drop steeply in stage 1; magenta 1000 °C falls fastest and reaches zero near ε ≈ 0.13; black 700 °C shows a small hump near the 2500 MPa level then decays; red 800 °C plateaus around the 1000–1500 MPa level over a long strain range and drops last near ε ≈ 0.28; blue 900 °C shows the highest sustained stage-2 hardening, a broad hump approaching the 3000 MPa gridline.

unreadable_items: panel (b): the numeric true-strain positions of the dashed S1/S2/S3 stage-boundary lines are not printed
panel (a) and (b): the terminal stress/strain values of the curves are not labelled numerically, so fracture strain and UTS can only be located relative to gridlines
